resources.string: Enter your masjid server address and the 6-digit code shown in Admin → Devices.
Enter the full https:// address shown in Admin → Devices.
That code didn\'t work. Generate a fresh code in Admin → Devices and try again.
Couldn\'t reach the server. Check the address, and that this tablet and the server are on the same Wi-Fi.
Couldn\'t secure the connection to the server. Ask an admin to check the setup.
Something went wrong. Please try again.
This tablet isn\'t locked down until it is paired, so you can leave at any time.
The server\'s security certificate changed, so this kiosk locked itself for safety. Pair it again to reconnect.
Ask a masjid admin if you don\'t have it.
That PIN wasn\'t right. Try again.
Too many attempts. Try again in %1$d seconds.
No exit PIN is set yet. Set one in Admin → Devices to protect this kiosk.

A USB card reader connects on its own — just plug it in. Use the button below only for a Bluetooth reader. No reader at all? Donors can still give: the kiosk offers typed card entry automatically whenever no reader is connected.
Updating the reader — keep it powered and nearby.
Finish Payments setup (Stripe account + a card-reader location) in the admin panel before connecting a reader.
Bluetooth and Location permission are needed to find a reader. Enable them for this app in the tablet\'s Settings, then try again.
Version %1$s is available (this kiosk is on %2$s).

Tapping Update app downloads the new version from your own masjid server and hands it straight to Android to install — no browser, and the kiosk comes back by itself. It needs \"Install apps from this kiosk\" in the list above; if that is off, Android will ask you to allow it first. Should the download fail, the kiosk falls back to opening the link in this tablet\'s browser.
To leave kiosk mode, set an exit PIN in Admin → Devices, then unlock with it. This keeps the kiosk locked until the PIN reaches this tablet.
Keeps the notification shade closed while the kiosk is locked.

Optional. While the kiosk is locked, this closes the notification shade / quick-settings the moment it is pulled down, so a donor can\'t reach settings from it. It reads no screen content and does nothing when the kiosk is unlocked (maintenance) or unpaired. Turn it on for the strongest lock without a computer.

Once the list above is green this tablet is set up without needing a computer: the kiosk is the Home app, so Home returns to the giving screen, and it reopens itself if anything sends it to the background. Hide the navigation bar in the tablet\'s own Settings (see below) to take away the Back, Home and Recents buttons, and turn on the shade lock above to keep the notification shade shut. An even stronger, fully un-leavable lock is available with the one-time device-owner setup in docs/TABLET_SETUP.md, but it is optional.
Everything this kiosk asks the tablet for. Tap a button and Android opens the right dialog or settings page, then the kiosk carries on where it left off when you come back.

Android won\'t show the dialog again on this tablet — it has been declined too many times. Turn it on by hand instead: the button below opens this app\'s settings, where you tap Permissions and allow it.

Lets the kiosk update itself: it downloads the new version from your own masjid server and hands it straight to Android to install, so nobody has to fetch an APK in a browser. Android calls this \"Install unknown apps\".
Needed to find and connect a Stripe Reader M2 wirelessly. Not needed if the reader is plugged in by USB, or if this kiosk takes cards by typing them in.
Stripe\'s reader software requires this before it will look for ANY card reader — over USB just as much as over Bluetooth. The kiosk never uses it to track where the tablet is.
The tablet\'s own location switch has to be on as well as the permission above, or no card reader can be found.
Turn Bluetooth on to use a Stripe Reader M2 wirelessly. Leave it off if the reader is connected by USB cable — the kiosk works either way.
Makes this the tablet\'s Home app, so pressing Home returns to the giving screen instead of an Android desktop, and the kiosk starts itself again after a reboot or a power cut.
Optional extra: shuts the notification shade again if it is ever pulled down. Enable \"OpenMasjid Kiosk — shade lock\" under Settings → Accessibility → Installed apps.
This tablet is provisioned as device owner, so the kiosk is locked completely: no status bar, no notification shade, no Home and no Recents. Only the exit PIN gets out.

Not set up, and not required — everything above works without it. This is the strongest lock and it removes the status bar entirely, but it needs a one-time setup from a computer on a factory-reset tablet. See docs/TABLET_SETUP.md.

To finish locking the tablet down, hide the system bars in the tablet's own Settings. The wording differs by manufacturer:

• BOTTOM NAVIGATION BAR — Settings → Display → Navigation bar (or System → Gestures), and choose "Gesture navigation" / "Swipe gestures". That removes the Back, Home and Recents buttons. Some tablets also offer a small pin icon that keeps the bar hidden until you swipe.

• TOP NOTIFICATION BAR — Android gives an ordinary app no way to remove this, and no tablet setting hides it. The optional shade lock above closes it the moment it is pulled down. Removing the bar completely needs the one-time device-owner setup in docs/TABLET_SETUP.md, which the kiosk then does for you automatically.

This tablet is device owner, so the kiosk already removes the status bar and blocks Home and Recents itself whenever the giving screen is showing — there is nothing to turn off in Settings. If you would also like the navigation bar gone outside the kiosk, set Settings → Display → Navigation bar to \"Gesture navigation\".
